# dependencytrack_workload_identity_binding (Resource)

Binds a workload identity to a Dependency-Track service account: tokens from `provider_name` whose `sub` claim matches `subject` (and whose claims satisfy `condition`, if set) can be exchanged for a session of the service account. Bindings cannot be modified: changing any argument replaces the binding. Requires Dependency-Track 5.2 or newer and the `ACCESS_MANAGEMENT` permission.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dependencytrack_service_account" "ci" {
  name = "ci-pipeline"
}

resource "dependencytrack_workload_identity_provider" "github_actions" {
  name     = "github-actions"
  type     = "OIDC"
  issuer   = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
  audience = "https://dtrack.example.com"
}

# Let workflows of acme/app on main act as the ci-pipeline service account.
resource "dependencytrack_workload_identity_binding" "app_main" {
  service_account = dependencytrack_service_account.ci.name
  provider_name   = dependencytrack_workload_identity_provider.github_actions.name
  subject         = "repo:acme/app:*"
  condition       = "claims.ref == \"refs/heads/main\""
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `provider_name` (String) The name of the workload identity provider whose tokens to trust
- `service_account` (String) The name of the service account (without the `svc:` prefix)
- `subject` (String) The `sub` claim to match, such as `repo:acme/app:ref:refs/heads/main`. A trailing `*` makes it a prefix match; the prefix must not be empty and must end with `:` or `/`, such as `repo:acme/app:*`

### Optional

- `condition` (String) A CEL expression over the token's claims (the `claims` map) that must evaluate to `true`, such as `claims.ref == "refs/heads/main"`. Use it when the subject alone cannot express the rule

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the binding in the format `service_account/uuid`
- `uuid` (String) The UUID of the binding

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Workload identity bindings can be imported using service_account/uuid.
terraform import dependencytrack_workload_identity_binding.example ci-pipeline/01a173cb-edbb-7928-9fc2-2d284001483a
```
